sentences.en: On Wednesday morning in Washington, the scene outside of the Supreme Court captured the enormous stakes of the case that was about to be argued before its nine justices.
sentences.zh: 周三上午在华盛顿，最高法院外的场景捕捉到了即将在这九位大法官面前辩论的案件所涉及的巨大赌注。

sentences.en: This is pivotal.
sentences.zh: 这至关重要。

sentences.en: This will define the immigration experience for decades.
sentences.zh: 这将决定未来几十年的移民体验。

sentences.en: Birthright citizenship has just been a big part of, like, what it means to be American for a very long time, like, almost as long as the country.
sentences.zh: 出生公民权长期以来一直是美国身份认同的重要组成部分，几乎和这个国家一样久远。

sentences.en: The crux of this is illegals or those here temporarily shouldn't receive the benefit of American citizenship, which is to be cherished.
sentences.zh: 此案的核心在于，非法移民或临时居留者不应享有美国公民身份带来的福利，这种身份是弥足珍贵的。

sentences.en: A case about President Trump's efforts to end birthright citizenship that literally asks who gets to be an American.
sentences.zh: 这是一起关于特朗普总统试图终结出生公民权的案件，它直截了当地提出了谁才有资格成为美国人的问题。

sentences.en: So this case was very important for me because I'm an immigrant, too.
sentences.zh: 所以这个案子对我来说非常重要，因为我也是一名移民。

sentences.en: We all came for a reason because the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这里都是有原因的，因为美国

sentences.en: is a shining city on the hill.
sentences.zh: 是一座山巅之城。

sentences.en: And now to change the whole thing, I'm like, did I make a right decision of wanting to come here?
sentences.zh: 而现在要改变这一切，我在想，我当初决定来这里是对的吗？

sentences.en: And a case so historic that President Trump himself showed up in the courtroom to hear the arguments.
sentences.zh: 这起案件具有历史意义，以至于特朗普总统本人亲自出现在法庭上听取辩论。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Anne Marimo takes us inside the room.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事安妮·马里莫将带我们走进法庭内部。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, April 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月2日，星期四。

sentences.en: Anne, you had a pretty coveted seat inside the Supreme Court on Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 安妮，周三上午你在最高法院里有一个令人垂涎的席位。

sentences.en: And I suspect your eyes quickly fixed themselves on the presence of President Trump.
sentences.zh: 我猜你的目光很快就锁定在了特朗普总统身上。

sentences.en: Yes, it was a historic day.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是历史性的一天。

sentences.en: The first sitting president to be in the Supreme Court courtroom for an oral argument and to be sitting there as the justices were debating birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 这是首位在任总统出现在最高法院法庭听取口头辩论，并坐在那里旁听大法官们辩论出生公民权问题。

sentences.en: And what did it look like for him to enter that august room?
sentences.zh: 他走进那个庄严的房间时是什么样子？

sentences.en: So a hush came over the courtroom as the president was escorted to his seat.
sentences.zh: 当总统被护送至座位时，法庭内一片寂静。

sentences.en: The courtroom is always quiet, but this was even more quiet than usual as he walked in at that moment wearing a red tie and a dark suit and took his seat.
sentences.zh: 法庭通常都很安静，但他那一刻走进来时，系着红领带，穿着深色西装，坐到座位上时，比平时更加安静。

sentences.en: And it's really interesting where he was seated.
sentences.zh: 而且他坐的位置非常有趣。

sentences.en: Instead of being close to the justices in the special seats reserved for their families and visiting dignitaries, he was seated in the front row for the public.
sentences.zh: 他没有坐在靠近大法官的、为家属和到访政要预留的特殊席位上，而是坐在了公众席的第一排。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: I think it's because he is one of the parties in the cases and he's not a lawyer or member of the Supreme Court bar.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为他是案件当事人之一，而不是律师或最高法院律师协会的成员。

sentences.en: So there he was in the front row of the public gallery.
sentences.zh: 所以他就坐在公众席的第一排。

sentences.en: Just far enough away, perhaps, for some of the justices liking.
sentences.zh: 也许离某些大法官喜欢的距离刚好够远。

sentences.en: It feels difficult to overstate the symbolic potency of the head of the executive branch being in this room, in the heart of the judicial branch.
sentences.zh: 行政部门首脑出现在司法部门的核心地带，这种象征意义怎么强调都不为过。

sentences.en: And as you know well, this is a president known for very keenly understanding power and how you flex it.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，这位总统以极其敏锐地理解权力和如何运用权力而闻名。

sentences.en: And it felt to me anyway like the president, by showing up for these oral arguments on this case, was basically saying, you all want to sit in judgment of my executive order on
sentences.zh: 在我看来，总统出席此案的口头辩论，基本上是在说：你们都想审判我的行政命令，关于

sentences.en: birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 出生公民权的。

sentences.en: And therefore, I'm going to sit in judgment of you as you do that.
sentences.zh: 因此，在你们审判的同时，我也要审判你们。

sentences.en: There's absolutely a lot of symbolism having him there.
sentences.zh: 他出现在那里绝对具有很多象征意义。

sentences.en: He had mused about showing up previously when the court took up his tariffs plan.
sentences.zh: 当法院审理他的关税计划时，他曾考虑过出席。

sentences.en: That was also very important to the president.
sentences.zh: 那对总统来说也非常重要。

sentences.en: He ended up not coming and saying he didn't want to be a distraction.
sentences.zh: 他最终没有来，说他不想造成干扰。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你是对的。

sentences.en: There's been this effort, as you've seen, when the court has ruled against him.
sentences.zh: 正如你所见，当法院做出对他不利的裁决时，一直有这种努力。

sentences.en: The president has tried to intimidate the justices and criticize them in really harsh personal terMs.
sentences.zh: 总统试图恐吓大法官，并以非常严厉的个人措辞批评他们。

sentences.en: So to have him actually there in person, face to face with the justices, sent a real signal.
sentences.zh: 所以他亲自到场，与大法官面对面，发出了一个真正的信号。

sentences.en: And above all, that signal was, this case is really important to the president and to his second term agenda, especially immigration.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，这个信号是：此案对总统及其第二任期议程，特别是移民问题，确实非常重要。

sentences.en: Just briefly remind us how this case found its way into this room.
sentences.zh: 请简要提醒我们这个案子是如何进入这个法庭的。

sentences.en: So you'll remember the president, on his first day back in office, issued this executive
sentences.zh: 你还记得总统在重返办公室的第一天，就发布了这项行政

sentences.en: order to really limit the guarantee of birthright citizenship and say, it does not include the children of illegal immigrants or the children of many temporary foreign visitors.
sentences.zh: 命令，旨在严格限制出生公民权的保障，并称其不包括非法移民的子女或许多临时外国访客的子女。

sentences.en: That was seen as an open challenge to the long-held understanding of the 14th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 这被视为对第14修正案长期以来理解的公开挑战。

sentences.en: And there were lawsuits filed immediately by Democratic state attorney generals and expected parents.
sentences.zh: 民主党州检察长和准父母们立即提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Basically saying the 14th Amendment guarantees that anyone born, with very few exceptions, on American soil is an American citizen.
sentences.zh: 基本上是说第14修正案保证了除极少数例外情况外，任何在美国领土上出生的人都是美国公民。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And not just in the 14th Amendment, but in subsequent court rulings, in actions by past presidents.
sentences.zh: 不仅是在第14修正案中，在随后的法院裁决和历任总统的行动中也是如此。

sentences.en: This has been the common, settled law understanding.
sentences.zh: 这已成为普遍且确定的法律共识。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so we always understood that the administration's legal arguments in defense of this executive order were going to be potentially tough sledding before the entire judiciary.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直明白，政府为捍卫这项行政命令所做的法律辩护，在整个司法机构面前可能会举步维艰。

sentences.en: So take us into these oral arguments and how they unfold.
sentences.zh: 那么带我们了解一下这些口头辩论以及它们是如何展开的。

sentences.en: And let's start with the administration's lawyer.
sentences.zh: 让我们从政府的律师开始。

sentences.en: We will hear argument this morning in case 25365, Trump versus Barbara.
sentences.zh: 我们现在听取25365号案件，特朗普诉芭芭拉案的辩论。

sentences.en: General Sauer?
sentences.zh: 索尔总检察长？

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法庭请允许。

sentences.en: President Trump's Solicitor General, John Sauer, who represents the administration at the
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统的副总检察长约翰·索尔，他在

sentences.en: Supreme Court as asking the justices to reinterpret or restore what he says is the original meaning of the 14th Amendment?
sentences.zh: 最高法院代表政府，要求大法官重新解释或恢复他所说的第14修正案的原始含义？

sentences.en: The citizenship clause was adopted just after the Civil War to grant citizenship to the newly freed slaves and their children.
sentences.zh: 公民权条款是在内战后通过的，旨在授予新获得自由的奴隶及其子女公民身份。

sentences.en: So a key point to the administration's argument centered on the language of the 14th Amendment and the meaning of a phrase, subject to the jurisdiction of.
sentences.zh: 因此，政府论点的关键点集中在第14修正案的措辞以及“受其管辖”这一短语的含义上。

sentences.en: The language of the 14th Amendment says that all persons born or naturalized in the United
sentences.zh: 第14修正案的措辞规定，所有在美国出生或入籍的人，

sentences.en: States and subject to the jurisdiction thereof are citizens of the United States.
sentences.zh: 并受其管辖的人，均为美国公民。

sentences.en: In 1884, this court recognized that subject to the jurisdiction means owing direct and immediate allegiance.
sentences.zh: 1884年，本院认定“受其管辖”意味着效忠于直接且即时的管辖权。

sentences.en: The clause, thus, does not extend citizenship to the children of temporary visa holders or illegal aliens.
sentences.zh: 因此，该条款并未将公民身份延伸至临时签证持有者或非法外国人的子女。

sentences.en: John Sauer is trying to get the justices to focus on, again, the meaning of subject to the jurisdiction of.
sentences.zh: 约翰·索尔试图让大法官们再次关注“受其管辖”的含义。

sentences.en: In his view, the babies of illegal immigrants are not subject to the jurisdiction of the
sentences.zh: 在他看来，非法移民的婴儿不受

sentences.en: United States and are therefore not citizens.
sentences.zh: 美国的管辖，因此不是公民。

sentences.en: Unrestricted birthright citizenship contradicts the practice of the overwhelming majority of modern nations.
sentences.zh: 不受限制的出生公民权与绝大多数现代国家的做法相矛盾。

sentences.en: It demeans the priceless and profound gift of American citizenship.
sentences.zh: 它贬低了美国公民身份这份无价而深远的礼物。

sentences.en: And why, according to Sauer, the president's solicitor general, is that the case, that children
sentences.zh: 那么，根据总统的副总检察长索尔的说法，为什么情况是这样，即非法移民所生子女

sentences.en: born to illegal immigrants are not subject to the jurisdiction thereof of the United States
sentences.zh: 不受美国政府管辖，

sentences.en: government and therefore not eligible to be American citizens when they're born on American soil?
sentences.zh: 因此在他们出生在美国领土上时没有资格成为美国公民？

sentences.en: So, the administration's argument really rests on one of the court's rulings in 1898, and this is the case of Wong Kim Ark.
sentences.zh: 政府的论点确实基于法院1898年的一项裁决，即黄锦阿克案（Wong Kim Ark）。

sentences.en: There, the court ruled that a man born in San Francisco, but to Chinese immigrants, was a citizen.
sentences.zh: 在该案中，法院裁定一名在旧金山出生但父母为中国移民的男子是公民。

sentences.en: And John Sauer says, we've been thinking about that case all wrong.
sentences.zh: 约翰·索尔说，我们一直以来对那个案子的理解都错了。

sentences.en: It's been read too broadly to apply to a larger group of people, and really, he says the key in that decision is the word domicile and the fact that Mr. Wong's parents were legally
sentences.zh: 它被解读得太宽泛，以至于适用于更大范围的人群。他说，该裁决的关键在于“住所”（domicile）一词，以及黄先生的父母在法律上

sentences.en: present in the United States, even though they were not citizens.
sentences.zh: 存在于美国的事实，尽管他们不是公民。

sentences.en: They had a commitment to living in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们有在美国居住的承诺。

sentences.en: And for that reason, when their son was born in San Francisco, he was a citizen.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他们的儿子在旧金山出生时，他就是公民。

sentences.en: The court says at the very beginning of his opinion, here are the accepted facts.
sentences.zh: 法院在意见书的开头就说，这是公认的事实。

sentences.en: These are lawfully domiciled here.
sentences.zh: 这些人是合法居住在这里的。

sentences.en: When it states the question presented, it talks about domicile.
sentences.zh: 当它陈述提出的问题时，谈到了住所。

sentences.en: When it recites the legal principle at page 693, it says domicile three times.
sentences.zh: 当它在第693页引用法律原则时，提到了三次住所。

sentences.en: And at page 705, at the end of the opinion, it says, here's the single question we've decided.
sentences.zh: 在第705页，意见书的结尾，它说，这是我们决定的唯一问题。

sentences.en: We've decided that Chinese immigrants with a permanent domicile in residence here are followed in the role of birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 我们决定，在中国移民拥有永久住所的情况下，他们遵循出生公民权的角色。

sentences.en: And so throughout the argument, John Sauer asked the justices to focus on that word in saying that that's key to someone being able to become a birthright citizen.
sentences.zh: 因此，在整个辩论过程中，约翰·索尔要求大法官们关注那个词，称那是某人能够成为出生公民权持有者的关键。

sentences.en: And just to find that word domicile, because having watched these oral arguments myself, not in the room, but at home, it comes up a lot.
sentences.zh: 为了定义“住所”这个词，因为我自己看过这些口头辩论，不是在现场，而是在家里，它经常出现。

sentences.en: It did come up a lot.
sentences.zh: 确实经常出现。

sentences.en: And the solicitor general told the justices domicile to him and in the law means somebody's
sentences.zh: 副总检察长告诉大法官们，对他而言以及在法律上，住所意味着某人的

sentences.en: residence, but also their intention to stay and make a home and having the ability legally to be able to be domiciled somewhere.
sentences.zh: 居住地，但也包括他们留下来安家的意图，以及在法律上有能力在某处拥有住所。

sentences.en: And in his telling, undocumented immigrants, by definition, cannot be legally domiciled in the United States because they are here illegally.
sentences.zh: 按照他的说法，无证移民根据定义不能在法律上在美国拥有住所，因为他们是非法在这里的。

sentences.en: Because they've come into the country illegally.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是非法进入这个国家的。

sentences.en: But also he brings in another term, and that is allegiance, because they sort of have a political allegiance to a foreign nation.
sentences.zh: 但他还引入了另一个术语，即“效忠”，因为他们某种程度上对外国有政治效忠。

sentences.en: It did not grant citizenship to the children of temporary visitors or illegal aliens who have no such allegiance.
sentences.zh: 它并未授予那些没有这种效忠的临时访客或非法外国人的子女公民身份。

sentences.en: So basically, Sauer is arguing that if you look really closely, especially at that ARC case
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，索尔是在辩称，如果你仔细观察，特别是最高法院在许多许多年前做出的那个阿克案（ARC）

sentences.en: issued by the Supreme Court many, many, many decades ago, people have been misunderstanding
sentences.zh: 裁决，人们长期以来一直误解了

sentences.en: this birthright citizenship precedent for a very long time, and they've allowed it to be applied too broadly to people who should not be birthright citizens, illegal immigrants
sentences.zh: 这个出生公民权的先例，他们允许它被太宽泛地应用于那些不应该成为出生公民权持有者的人，特别是非法移民。

sentences.en: especially.
sentences.zh: 尤其是。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So how do the justices respond to this argument?
sentences.zh: 那么大法官们是如何回应这一论点的？

sentences.en: So John Sauer got a lot of pushback pretty quickly, including from some of the key conservative justices who are often in the majority, most notably from Chief Justice Roberts.
sentences.zh: 约翰·索尔很快就遭到了很多反驳，包括来自一些经常处于多数派地位的关键保守派大法官，最著名的是首席大法官罗伯茨。

sentences.en: You obviously put a lot of weight on subject to the jurisdiction thereof, but the examples you give to support that strike me as very quirky.
sentences.zh: 你显然非常看重“受其管辖”这一条，但你用来支持这一点的例子在我看来非常古怪。

sentences.en: Who referred to the government's theory as quirky?
sentences.zh: 谁把政府的理论称为古怪？

sentences.en: Never a great sign.
sentences.zh: 这从来都不是一个好兆头。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So the Chief Justice pointed out that the 14th Amendment includes very specific exceptions to groups of people who are not subject to the jurisdiction of the United States and
sentences.zh: 所以首席大法官指出，第14修正案包含了针对某些群体非常具体的例外，这些人不受美国管辖，

sentences.en: therefore not citizens.
sentences.zh: 因此不是公民。

sentences.en: You know, children of ambassadors, children of enemies during a hostile invasion, children on warships.
